_comment: Phase 3 - Territory, step 1: the village's stores (food, wood, stone; gold is the house treasury) and building. The player places important buildings from the Build menu; villagers raise them; a Master of Works speeds every site. All tuning lives here.

resources.name: Food
resources.description: Grain, bread and greens. Everyone eats every day; an empty granary makes the village miserable.

resources.name: Wood
resources.description: Timber for building and firewood for every hearth.

resources.name: Stone
resources.description: Cut stone for foundations and walls. Build a Stonecutter's Yard to quarry it.

resources.name: Cloth
resources.description: Woollen cloth from the village's looms, spun from its own flocks' wool. The realm's richest trade.

resources.name: Ironware
resources.description: Nails, tools and fittings from the smith's forge, which burns charcoal.

resources.name: Ale
resources.description: Ale brewed at the tavern from the village's grain. Its price follows bread's.

resources.name: Gold
resources.description: Your house's treasury (rents, dues and wages).

storage._comment: Most of each resource the village can hold: base + bonus for every finished building of a type. wares: the same for cloth, ironware and ale (Phase 6.2).

crafts._comment: Phase 6.2: craftsmen turn the stores into wares, per worker per day at normal productivity: 'makes' per_day of a ware from 'uses' of the stores. A craft only works a store's surplus: never below reserve_days of what the village itself eats and burns (more than the 10 days' bread that draws settlers, growth food_days_good), nor below reserve_share of the store's room, kept for building (the alewife stops brewing in a lean year, the smith when the woodpile is low); with too little, it makes what it can.

production._comment: Per worker per day at normal productivity. Builders on a construction site produce nothing that day.

productivity._comment: Worker output multiplier: happiness 0 -> min, 100 -> max; traits multiply.

seasons._comment: Food output by season: fields lie fallow in winter, the harvest comes in autumn.

construction._comment: Work is counted in builder-hours. Each builder adds their rate for every hour of their work shift; the Master of Works multiplies everything.

placement._comment: Meters. New buildings snap beside a road and face it; lanes are laid automatically from the door to the nearest road. Nothing is built in the manor's forecourt (manor_clear around its door). yard_names: the yards (layout props) a building may not stand on anywhere in their footprint, nor its lane cross, and what the Build panel calls them.

hiring._comment: Who takes the jobs at a finished building, in order of preference. Adults only.

homes._comment: Homes grow on their own (step 2). Each family lives in its own home. When every home is full, the village builds a cottage beside a main road; homes whose needs are met are upgraded by adding floors. Rent is gold per day for each lived-in home at that level.
homes._lodgers: Townhouses (tier 2) take in lodgers as the settlement grows: families a Townhouse can hold, by charter (Hamlet, Village, Market Town, Town). Lodgers pay rent too: towns grow denser, not only wider.

needs.label: 5 days of food in the granary
A chapel or tavern within 60 m
Lived here 8 days as a Timber House
10 days of food in the granary
Both a chapel and a tavern within 75 m

growth._comment: New families settle when the village is appealing and a home stands empty. Appeal fills the settler bar each day (appeal x progress_per_appeal); at 100 a family arrives. Families walk in along a road from the edge of the map.
growth._max_population: How many may live here is set by the settlement's charter (data/charters.json).

auto._comment: Homes and upgrades the village orders by itself. They never spend below the reserve, so your own orders keep their materials.

buildable.name: Stonecutter's Yard
buildable.description: Stonecutters haul and dress stone from the hills. The village's only source of stone.

buildable.name: Woodcutters' Lodge
buildable.description: Two more woodcutters fell timber in the forest.

buildable.name: Weavers' Workshop
buildable.description: Two weavers work looms here, weaving cloth from the wool the village's flocks give. Cloth is the realm's richest trade.

buildable.name: Smithy
buildable.description: A smith at the forge makes nails, tools and fittings from bar iron, burning charcoal (wood).

buildable.name: Farmstead
buildable.description: A farmer and a farmhand work new fields around the house.

buildable.name: Granary
buildable.description: Raises how much food, wood and stone the village can store.

buildable.name: Bakery
buildable.description: A baker turns flour into bread for the village.

buildable.name: Tavern
buildable.description: Ale, warmth and gossip. Homes need a tavern near them to grow, and villagers gather there in the evening.

buildable.name: Chapel
buildable.description: A place to pray. Homes need a chapel near them to grow, and the devout visit it.

buildable.name: Market Hall
buildable.description: An arcaded hall where merchants trade: gold every day, settlers drawn by market days, and a market for nearby Townhouses.
